ra: Hesiod, Theog. 306-308: Echidna couples with Typhon (Typhaon) to bear the monster brood. paired_with (not consort_of, which is not a valid type).
Hesiod, Theog. 309-310: Echidna bore Orthrus the hound of Geryon.
Hesiod, Theog. 310-312: Echidna bore Cerberus, the brazen-voiced hound of Hades (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 313-315: Echidna bore the Lernaean Hydra (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 319-325: the Chimera in the prevailing reading belongs to the Echidna/Typhon line (variant: of Echidna and Orthrus). Existing entity.
Hesiod, Theog. 306-310: Typhon father of Echidna's brood, including Orthrus.
Hesiod, Theog. 306-312: Typhon father of Cerberus by Echidna (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 306-315: Typhon father of the Hydra by Echidna (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 309-312: Orthrus and Cerberus both born of Typhon and Echidna (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 309-311; Apollodorus 2.5.10: Orthrus guarded the cattle of Geryon and was slain by Heracles (existing entity).
Hesiod, Theog. 326-327: the Sphinx (Phix) born of Orthrus (contested maternal line).
Hesiod, Theog. 326-329: the Sphinx and Nemean Lion born of the Chimera (by Orthrus) per one construal. Existing entity.
Hesiod, Theog. 327-329: the Nemean Lion in the same brood-line, connected to the Chimera/Orthrus. Both existing entities.
Poetic Edda, Grímnismál 32, 35 and Völuspá 66: Níðhöggr gnaws the root of Yggdrasil from below (existing entity).

Modern comparative cross-tradition pairing: Níðhöggr as the Norse functional cognate of the Greek chthonic monster-serpent of the Echidna brood (aligned_with = modern functional analogue, not ancient identification).

Structural grouping within the wider chthonic Phorcys/Ceto and sea-monster cohort of early Greek myth (Gantz, Early Greek Myth); cohort linkage, NOT attested kinship (changed from sibling_of, which would falsely assert shared parentage).
Structural contrast among Gaia's primordial earth-born hosts: the Hundred-Handers fight for Zeus, while the Gigantes war against the Olympians (Hesiod, Theog.; Apollodorus 1.6).
Comparative grouping of monstrous bird-collectives of Greek myth (Stymphalian Birds, Harpies, Sirens); cohort linkage for graph connectivity, not genealogical kinship.
